name: Nashville Charm
description: 30 day plus rental - book for one month and then discuss longer rental option. Turn of century bungalow in East Nashville with city park, greenway and river behind house. Walk to shops, eateries and music venues. Downtown located 19 blocks away.  Rental unit is accessed through front door of home and located on second floor. The furnished space includes a combined sitting room with desk, kitchenette and wardrobe, a master bath with jacuzzi and shower, and a small bedroom with double bed.
host_about: My husband and I are parents of 5 grown children, living in various places in the US attending school/working. We've lived in East Nashville for 20 years. My husband, Collier, is a recently retired public defender and I am self-employed, having previously worked with various non-profit organizations and continuing to mediate and write. Most of my non-profit work was with community-based economic development organizations, racial and social justice groups, mentally and physically challenged people and women-focused efforts. We especially like activists, artists, adventurers and visionaries, but anyone wanting to travel to Nashville and get a real feel for our small town/ city and its friendly inhabitants would be happy staying with us. We live a simple life and believe in radical hospitality because we are all visitors in this world.

description:

name: ButterflyRoom-queen room, private bath
description: Morningstar House! Extended stay - 3+ months- it’s a clean, peaceful fully furnished private room and bath with all utilities, wifi, w/d, supplies, stocked kitchen .. just bring clothes and you are home! Great for a retreat, work or soft landing place for your move to Nashville. Just 10 miles from downtown, yet quiet place near the lake! More options? Contact me and I will help you find a room either in my home, or with friends in different parts of city.  Let’s talk! : )
host_about:
For 35 years I was serving the world as a community organizer, artist, expressive arts facilitator, and traveler and then in for 20 years lived in a very large, beautiful home near Nashville with plenty of space for welcoming the world at the Morningstar House, before moving back to my hometown in southern Tennessee.  I have a passion for community building across lines of race, class, and culture and have found work on the boards and staff of many church and community non-profit organizations, locally, regionally and internationally.

I am the oldest grandchild in a large farm family in Southern Tennessee and learned the fine art of hospitality from my ancestors, especially warm-hearted grandmothers and great-grandmothers.  There was a great synergy and sustainability in the collective, cooperative work of my large family, and in the 15 years I lived in the "city" I brought this ethic and value to my life in community there.  

After 10 years of leadership in the forms of InterPlay, we formed and were practicing with MorningStar Community Arts, linking arts and social transformation, writing, and performing. I've written poetry all along the journey and am currently publishing an extensive audio collection with a title something like:  Radical Hospitality: Grief, Grace and Grits. 

I love to travel and have been to Morocco several times to stay with extended family there. Hawaii and Australia are favorites, too. I have 3 teenage grandchildren who grew up in the “red house” next to my “blue house” and now both houses are fully open for sharing extended stays with long term residents.  The houses are equipped for children of every age with art supplies, books, music, games, movies, etc.   

I always loved hosting house concerts, circle gatherings, and potlucks in my home and am enjoying taking this longtime  practice of hosting friends and family in my home to a new level with airbnb and other networks by hosting strangers that very often become friends. Since mid 2015, we made the shift at the Morningstar House to host guests for a 30 day minimum stay, so there's more continuity and just 3-4 guests sharing this huge home at any time. 
I spent 20 years traveling the world with my cultural work and my favorite way to visit any city is by doing a creative homestay with hosts that were sometimes friends, and sometimes friends of friends.  It's such a sweet way to come to know a city by having a safe, friendly, homey landing place. So that's what I want to offer now.  The spirit of hospitality comes naturally and easy to me.  My family used to say "I never met a stranger"  I really enjoy people in all their variety and would be happy to provide you a good balance of quiet and private time, and also friendly, helpful support as you encounter Nashville.

The new owner of my daughters “red house” Marquetta Dupree will be starting to offer expressive arts facilitation and support to guests interested in that, and possibly even collaborate with guests to create concerts, workshops and other events in the PlayRoom which holds about 55 people for a concert, and 30 for workshops.  For an affordable and hospitable way to live for your time in Nashville come and be a part of this community.

life motto:  "Sometimes you just have to take a leap and build your wings on the way down"..

See website at Morningstar Arts dot net.

name: A+ Carriage House & Courtyard! 5 mins to Downtown
description: Gorgeous carriage house with private entry, courtyard, parking and all you need to enjoy a few days in Nashville! But the best part - Only mins to downtown! 8 mins by car. PERMIT # 500566
host_about:
I know your not coming to Nashville to visit me, but i will do my best to provide a great place to stay while you are in Nashville! I am a single Dad with 2 great kids off to college! I built this home 3 years ago and love living near downtown Nashville. I am an avid walker and most weeks put in 15 to 20 miles just walking from my home to the Historical Germantown area, Bicentennial Mall State Park, Farmers Market, State Capital, Legislative Plaza, TPAC, then on to Lower Broad, 2nd Ave, and Riverfront park where all the honky tonks are located! That total distance is just a little over 2 miles each way. 

     I was in the USAF and Tennessee Air Guard for 13 years where i was a navigator on C-130's. After my military life i became a General Contractor and started my own business. After being in the country for so long i decided to try the city life. I bought a vacant lot in this historical overlay district and loved it. Since then I have built 2 more homes on this street.

     I also love to hike the mountains! I have summed 3 12,000 foot peaks in the Rockies and last summer my son and I summed 14,254 foot Long's Peak in Rocky Mountain National Park. I must admit - it kicked my ass ... but wow!... what a view!  Leaves no doubt there is a God!  I also love to kayak and travel. But the best times are with the kids. We love to play strategy board games..Settlers of Catan, Acquire, and Cashflow. I love Axis and Allies, but its hard to get them to play that! I also play in a Texas holdem Poker League...for points...not for cash!

UPDATE:  That's my first grandbaby...Walt!
UPDATE:  Angel's Landing hike at Zion National Park!!

name: Affordable extended stays,  OPEN NOW
description: New photos soon! Coming to Nashville for 30 days or more? We provide a safe, clean, comfortable space for your extended stay. Ideal for summer internships, work travel, and relocations. We have several options in the two houses side by side.. 4 bedrooms with shared baths plus an open, spacious loft. Affordable monthly rates starting at $1,100 with discounts possible for stays of 3 mo or more. Please inquire .. we can almost always find a place for you!
host_about:
For 35 years I was serving the world as a community organizer, artist, expressive arts facilitator, and traveler and then in for 20 years lived in a very large, beautiful home near Nashville with plenty of space for welcoming the world at the Morningstar House, before moving back to my hometown in southern Tennessee.  I have a passion for community building across lines of race, class, and culture and have found work on the boards and staff of many church and community non-profit organizations, locally, regionally and internationally.

I am the oldest grandchild in a large farm family in Southern Tennessee and learned the fine art of hospitality from my ancestors, especially warm-hearted grandmothers and great-grandmothers.  There was a great synergy and sustainability in the collective, cooperative work of my large family, and in the 15 years I lived in the "city" I brought this ethic and value to my life in community there.  

After 10 years of leadership in the forms of InterPlay, we formed and were practicing with MorningStar Community Arts, linking arts and social transformation, writing, and performing. I've written poetry all along the journey and am currently publishing an extensive audio collection with a title something like:  Radical Hospitality: Grief, Grace and Grits. 

I love to travel and have been to Morocco several times to stay with extended family there. Hawaii and Australia are favorites, too. I have 3 teenage grandchildren who grew up in the “red house” next to my “blue house” and now both houses are fully open for sharing extended stays with long term residents.  The houses are equipped for children of every age with art supplies, books, music, games, movies, etc.   

I always loved hosting house concerts, circle gatherings, and potlucks in my home and am enjoying taking this longtime  practice of hosting friends and family in my home to a new level with airbnb and other networks by hosting strangers that very often become friends. Since mid 2015, we made the shift at the Morningstar House to host guests for a 30 day minimum stay, so there's more continuity and just 3-4 guests sharing this huge home at any time. 
I spent 20 years traveling the world with my cultural work and my favorite way to visit any city is by doing a creative homestay with hosts that were sometimes friends, and sometimes friends of friends.  It's such a sweet way to come to know a city by having a safe, friendly, homey landing place. So that's what I want to offer now.  The spirit of hospitality comes naturally and easy to me.  My family used to say "I never met a stranger"  I really enjoy people in all their variety and would be happy to provide you a good balance of quiet and private time, and also friendly, helpful support as you encounter Nashville.

The new owner of my daughters “red house” Marquetta Dupree will be starting to offer expressive arts facilitation and support to guests interested in that, and possibly even collaborate with guests to create concerts, workshops and other events in the PlayRoom which holds about 55 people for a concert, and 30 for workshops.  For an affordable and hospitable way to live for your time in Nashville come and be a part of this community.

life motto:  "Sometimes you just have to take a leap and build your wings on the way down"..

name: Southern Charm meets Old World Hospitality
description: Walk along the brick path under the maple tree to the front porch and you will feel like you have gone back in time. Decorated with an Old World style with timeless pieces from all over the world.  Whatever your taste, you will feel at home in this beautiful and historic area of town. Located in the HEART of EVERYTHING, you will have easy access to all of Nashville's hot spots. This home is not just an AirBnB, but a hospitality experience in a comfortable, open and private luscious setting.
host_about:
I am very excited about sharing my home with you on AirBnB.  As you can see it is Southern Charm that meets Old World Hospitality.  I have traveled extensively, having worked for Delta Air Lines for 13+ years, and acquired a taste for European and Old World comfort and warmth.

Presently I am a realtor (and would be glad to help you in that arena in any way) and have lived in my home here 26+ years.  I have 4 grown children, who were raised here and they loved the yard, the creek, and of course their home.  We also love Nashville and feel very blessed to have lived in this location for so long.  I love flea markets and antique shops and treasure finding old, eclectic, and unique pieces that you will see scattered about.

My home is 4BR/4BA and the rooms are large.  If your party is smaller and needs less space, I am not opposed to renting just the downstairs which is 2BR/2BA so please don't pass my home by if this helps you.

As you will find out if you don't already know, we are close to "everything".  Downtown (8min), the airport (12min), Vanderbilt (7-8min), Belmont Univ (5-6 min), Lipscomb Univ (3-4min), the trendy 12th South Area (5-6 min), Green Hills (4-5 min) which includes The Green Hills Mall (the nicest mall in TN), Trader Joe's (my favorite), The Hill Center which has high end shops, Whole Foods, and many eateries.  Please note that these times are WITHOUT traffic.

I do hope you will have fun in Nashville and your time in my home will be a memorable experience and not just a place to sleep.  Come back soon.

name: Heidtke House, A Rare Find & Featured on TV!
description:
Please note - Heidtke House is only available for 30 nights minimum stay at this time.

Minutes from Downtown Nashville, Opryland, East Nashville, and top local eats, this popular retreat blends charm with modern comfort.

Perfect for up to 8 guests, it offers a private backyard oasis, superfast WiFi, and personalized recommendations from Nashville native hosts John and Ellen.
host_about:
I often joke with others that I am one of the 12 born-and-raised Nashvillians that still live in Nashville. 

I grew up on a working farm south of Franklin. A regular day on the farm involved raising horses, goats and going to fairs to show our award winning Shorthorn cattle. 
 
During college I became deeply involved in agricultural mechanics, and rebuilt numerous vehicles to run on ethanol, methane from cow manure, biodiesel from soybean oil, and hydrogen from water. 

To promote these  "southern-fried fuels", we drove these vehicles all the way up to Canada, and competed for speed records at the Bonneville Salt Flats. 

I am currently working as development director for a software company.  My hobbies involves renovating houses, gardening, cooking, and entertaining friends and family. 

My wife Ellen was born in China, a true city girl, her interests are more into fashion & Electrical Engineering. She tells everyone she came to the US to study high-voltage transmission, but I really think she came here to find my secret BBQ recipes and me. ☺ 

We love to travel together and have been to Beijing, Hong Kong, London, Vancouver...  Everywhere we go, we try to stay away from hotels, staying with locals is  way more interesting. 

Nashville is a very southern but also culturally diverse city, it offers amazing food and cultural experiences from across the globe. There are wonderful cultural events (many for free) and restaurants to explore. 

As a true local Nashvillean, I would Love to connect you with your special interests. We are available to interact with you as much or as little as you like. 

We love our city & community, and can’t wait to share it with you and help you have a fantastic visit to Nashville!

host_about:
For 35 years I was serving the world as a community organizer, artist, expressive arts facilitator, and traveler and then in for 20 years lived in a very large, beautiful home near Nashville with plenty of space for welcoming the world at the Morningstar House, before moving back to my hometown in southern Tennessee.  I have a passion for community building across lines of race, class, and culture and have found work on the boards and staff of many church and community non-profit organizations, locally, regionally and internationally.

I am the oldest grandchild in a large farm family in Southern Tennessee and learned the fine art of hospitality from my ancestors, especially warm-hearted grandmothers and great-grandmothers.  There was a great synergy and sustainability in the collective, cooperative work of my large family, and in the 15 years I lived in the "city" I brought this ethic and value to my life in community there.  

After 10 years of leadership in the forms of InterPlay, we formed and were practicing with MorningStar Community Arts, linking arts and social transformation, writing, and performing. I've written poetry all along the journey and am currently publishing an extensive audio collection with a title something like:  Radical Hospitality: Grief, Grace and Grits. 

I love to travel and have been to Morocco several times to stay with extended family there. Hawaii and Australia are favorites, too. I have 3 teenage grandchildren who grew up in the “red house” next to my “blue house” and now both houses are fully open for sharing extended stays with long term residents.  The houses are equipped for children of every age with art supplies, books, music, games, movies, etc.   

I always loved hosting house concerts, circle gatherings, and potlucks in my home and am enjoying taking this longtime  practice of hosting friends and family in my home to a new level with airbnb and other networks by hosting strangers that very often become friends. Since mid 2015, we made the shift at the Morningstar House to host guests for a 30 day minimum stay, so there's more continuity and just 3-4 guests sharing this huge home at any time. 
I spent 20 years traveling the world with my cultural work and my favorite way to visit any city is by doing a creative homestay with hosts that were sometimes friends, and sometimes friends of friends.  It's such a sweet way to come to know a city by having a safe, friendly, homey landing place. So that's what I want to offer now.  The spirit of hospitality comes naturally and easy to me.  My family used to say "I never met a stranger"  I really enjoy people in all their variety and would be happy to provide you a good balance of quiet and private time, and also friendly, helpful support as you encounter Nashville.

The new owner of my daughters “red house” Marquetta Dupree will be starting to offer expressive arts facilitation and support to guests interested in that, and possibly even collaborate with guests to create concerts, workshops and other events in the PlayRoom which holds about 55 people for a concert, and 30 for workshops.  For an affordable and hospitable way to live for your time in Nashville come and be a part of this community.

life motto:  "Sometimes you just have to take a leap and build your wings on the way down"..

See website at Morningstar Arts dot net.

description:
We survived tornadoes & COVID19. Welcome back!

Our home has unique architectural details and elegant furnishings in a casual and spacious setting where fun and relaxation are top priorities. We’re 5 minutes from Five Points, downtown Nashville, Music City Center, Bridgestone Arena, Ascend Amphitheater, the Schermerhorn, and lower Broadway, including the Country Music Hall of Fame, Ryman Auditorium, Tootsie’s, The Stage, and restaurants & dance halls galore.

host_about:
Welcome to Shelby House!  I am a native Nashvillian and Molly grew up nearby in Arkansas. After a couple of decades of career-related travel, we are fortunate to have resettled here. We love the city, especially East Nashville, and look forward to helping you explore our hometown. As East Nashville residents ourselves, we live close by and are happy to share our experiences about local haunts, happenings, and true faves. 

We've lived in the US and abroad and have traveled a lot. This property has all the qualities we love about get-a-way digs. It’s unique, well-built, and well-appointed. It’s close to everything you’d want to do yet sufficiently away from the crowd that relaxation and rejuvenation are foregone conclusions. It’s close to nature (a nature preserve, a local park, a river, the 14-mile Greenway) yet within walking distance to urban vibrancy.  Vacationers will love the funky elegance while longer-term renters may think of it as a second home, due to personal touches, such as a screen door, backyard flower gardens (seasonal), and photos of giggly family members who remind us of what’s important.

We have a lot of information to share! I will help you eat your way through Nashville at new – as well as long-established – restaurants while Molly will send you out and about to burn off the calories while enjoying Nashville's treasures. As much as possible, the home features the work of local artisans, small business owners, and other creative types who call Nashville or TN home.  We think Nashville offers something for most travelers, including but not limited to musicians and music lovers, writers, athletes, fashionistas, foodies, hobbyists/crafters, sports fans, conventioneers, families, couples, wine-or-beer enthusiasts, friends, girls' groups, guys' groups, outdoorsy folks, and corporate retreaters. We have access to people with unique talents and expertise, so let us know if we can help customize your trip!  We are members of the "Top 3%," a small group of hosts who donate up to 3% "off the top" to local non-profits. In 2018, we supported research on Giant Axonal Neuropathy (GAN). In 2019, Shelby House's contributions supported  military veterans.  In 2020, we're supporting veterans and affordable housing. Stay at Shelby House and help us give back.

name: Downtown Music City Loft living ~Steps to Broadway
description:
The Fancy Features:
* 1 bedroom, 1 king bed
* Sleeps 4
* 1 luxury sleeper sofa in the living room (queen size, sleeps 2)
* 1 full bathroom
* Free toiletries (shampoo, conditioner, body soap)
* Hair dryer
* Full kitchen and laundry room
* Standard coffee maker (we do not provide coffee) Starbucks right next door!

host_about:
Hey y'all! My name is Dani Dubetz and I created my short-term rental business in 2012. 

Prior to moving to Nashville, I played volleyball for Florida International University and later worked as a news reporter for WPTV in West Palm Beach. I learned telling a sad story every day wasn't really 'my thing.' 

I moved to Nashville, like many, in pursuit of a music career, working as a beverage cart girl at a golf club, waitressing and coaching volleyball. As humbling as it was to go from being on TV to paying my rent in $1 bills, I didn't regret my decision.

Unfortunately, I quickly realized that the talent in Music City was far beyond any I'd come across in South Florida and surely, more than I was capable of as a self-professed Karaoke Queen and front woman of my Florida cover band!

From 2009-2012 I bounced between jobs in search of my purpose, a career that would allow me to utilize my talents, gifts and creativity and make a positive impact. My mother was a successful 'house-flipper' in our small town, Lanexa, Virginia. She was gracious enough to teach me her business, in loving support to help me keep my head above water! I flipped one or two houses a year but was never quite successful enough where I didn't need a day job. In 2010 I went against my mother's advice and purchased a loft in downtown Nashville, intending to flip it.

I moved to Nashville, like many, in pursuit of a music career, working as a beverage cart girl at a golf club, waitressing and coaching volleyball. As humbling as it was to go from being on TV to paying my rent in $1 bills, I didn't regret my decision.

Unfortunately, I quickly realized that the talent in Music City was far beyond any I'd come across in South Florida and surely, more than I was capable of as a self-professed Karaoke Queen and front woman of my Florida cover band!

From 2009-2012 I bounced between jobs in search of my purpose, a career that would allow me to utilize my talents, gifts and creativity and make a positive impact. My mother was a successful 'house-flipper' in our small town, Lanexa, Virginia. She was gracious enough to teach me her business, in loving support to help me keep my head above water! I flipped one or two houses a year but was never quite successful enough where I didn't need a day job. In 2010 I went against my mother's advice and purchased a loft in downtown Nashville, intending to flip it. 

In my 27 year old mind, sleeping on an air mattress in an empty loft, spending my free time listening to music in the bars just two blocks away was a pretty sweet gig. I was naive and ignorant to the fact that… it was 2010! Downtown properties were foreclosing faster than they were being purchased. My brilliant idea turned into my first failed flip. Between that and getting fired from a few jobs, my confidence was completely wrecked. 

My mom helped me furnish the loft, thinking staging the property would help it sell. Meanwhile, an acquaintance mentioned she'd listed her house on a web site and was renting it out nightly. As all of my personal belongings were packed up to move back home, tail between my legs and head low in utter defeat and self-loathing, my mom convinced me to use the last available funds on my credit card to list the loft online and, 'You never know. Maybe if you get a reservation you can get by for a little longer until you find your next job?'

In hindsight, I realize I actually failed my way forward. As I still kept finding jobs that would call me back to Nashville, but less optimistic that any of them would stick, I practically lived out of my car. When my loft was rented, I slept on friends' couches. If my loft was rented and I was again unemployed, I would travel to real estate seminars to make the most of my time. Eventually I realized that the career I had been searching for — an opportunity to build and grow a brand — was being met by my loft. 

I set to work finding a way to purchase more lofts in the building. I was passionate about creating the 'authentic Nashville experience' for my guests by providing a space that featured work from local artists and thereby, helping support my community. 
This passion has grown into something far beyond what I ever dreamed for myself or imagined possible. I never wanted to be a boss, I just wanted a job and one that I loved! I now have an entire team that not only loves Nashville, but deeply cares about helping our guests get the most from their visit. 

Our cleaning team is top-notch, as they understand all of the marketing we do on the front end means nothing if you walk in and aren't completely blown away! Our security team, Asset, are former military guys who not only provide comfort for our guests entering the building after a late night on the town but are extremely professional and courteous. We think it's awesome to have our guests looked after by 'Captain America!' 

On the reservations side, we have rockstars who truly care about your upcoming visit whether it be for a vacation, reunion, bachelorette party or conference. We not only want to give you an amazing space to call home and help you experience Nashville like a local, but we want to give you customized recommendations and resources so you fall in love with our city and want to come back again and again!

Suzanne is the head boss of guest experiences. She has been with the company since the beginning and you truly will not find someone more passionate about Nashville and its music scene. You're in the best hands! 

A little about how Suzanne and I came to work together, because I absolutely love telling this story — In 2012-2013 we were roommates. I was visiting with banks all day, trying to convince them that #TeamMCL was something to believe in (which at the time, had never before been seen at such scale in Nashville) and staying up all night answering e-mails and fulfilling reservations. Suzanne walked out of her home office (mine was the kitchen table) to tell me she was cut from her company in a corporate downsizing. Realizing I needed to not only get some sleep, but keep whatever little funds I had in-house so we could avoid eviction, I asked her if she wanted to work for #TeamMCL. Her classic response, which I will always remember, a very unenthusiastic, 'I guess I have to.' 
It's so comical to remember that day because while she begrudgingly agreed then, she is a total rockstar now!

Suzanne has grown to not only be an irreplaceable teammate, to whom I am forever grateful to helping me make this business possible not only in operations, but in the emotional support that I needed when times were really hard and no bank would give me the time of day, my mother's passing and my first business partner's ALS diagnosis (Former Tennessee Titan, Tim Shaw. Check out his book 'Blitz Your Life' because it's GREAT!), but she is a true champion of #TeamMCL and the authentic Nashville experience we are trying to provide for our guests. She maintains the properties to a high standard of expectations and she delights in hearing our guests' stories, connecting with them and giving them personalized recommendations of shows and events. A recommendation from her is like getting the 'inside scoop' on up-and-coming artists, so you can feel like one of the 'cool kids' when you come to town and get to experience Nashville like a true local!

My vision for #TeamMCL is this:
We aim to create a world-wide brand of privately owned vacation rentals, starting with the Music City, USA. The industry of private home rentals is extremely variable and uncertain. I have traveled and stayed in homes all over and have asked these very same questions. I have collected my own terrible experiences where the property wasn't as advertised, wasn't clean or I didn't feel safe. I have also stayed in places that didn't feel authentic, but were stale and run-of-the-mill, where I may have just as well stayed in a box-store hotel chain! Overall, the property you stay in can significantly impact the quality of your trip, your emotions, adventure, experience and ultimately, your memories! Knowing this and what I've learned through my own experiences and from our guests since renting out my first loft in 2011 before establishing #TeamMCL as a company, I have a dream to bring a standard of comfort, quality and consistency into the vacation rental world, all while creating spaces that are 'authentic' to that city by supporting local artists and reflecting that city's unique culture and vibe. 

More than being a successful company with a culture we can be proud of, we intend to be a force for good. We feel it's our mission to give back to our guests by delivering an exceptional experience where our guests feel genuinely cared for, but as a company we aim to do so much more to positively impact the world. We want our guests to know that while they are getting what they pay for and having an amazing experience worthy of a 5-Star review, a portion of their hard earned money is being paid forward toward a cause, whether it's ALS research, disadvantaged and orphaned children, or teen moms needing additional career education and encouragement.

Having faced personal struggle and the challenges of starting a company, coming through victoriously to other side, I truly believe that anything is possible!

* Setting the stage — Owning romantic real estate in romantic cities, all over the world
* WOWing our guests with cleanliness, quality and customer service — Creating a world-wide brand of vacation rentals that travelers can trust
* WOWing our guests by delighting five of their senses (Sight, Smell, Touch, Taste and Sound) through our properties and personalized recommendations of authentic, unique and local experiences
* Be WOW Memory Makers — WOW our guests so they can experience joy, delight and adventure, through our properties and recommendations so they can create memories they will cherish for a lifetime when they Stay {Somewhere} Awesome!
* Positively impact our Team, our guests and our community through passion, growth/learning and contribution

Thank you, in advance, for giving us the opportunity to meet our goals as a team. We are looking forward to serving you and earning your 5-Star Review. We live and die by them. If there's anything you need from us during your stay, please contact us so we have the opportunity to deliver! Also, word-of-mouth is essential for us to grow and thrive so if you loved staying at a #TeamMCL loft, please tell your friends! 

With Sincerity and Deep Appreciation,
Dani Dubetz

* Unbeatable location: walking distance to everything in downtown Nashville, 1.5 blocks to Broadway (Honky Tonk row!!)
host_about:
Hey y'all! My name is Dani Dubetz and I created my short-term rental business in 2012. 

Prior to moving to Nashville, I played volleyball for Florida International University and later worked as a news reporter for WPTV in West Palm Beach. I learned telling a sad story every day wasn't really 'my thing.' 

I moved to Nashville, like many, in pursuit of a music career, working as a beverage cart girl at a golf club, waitressing and coaching volleyball. As humbling as it was to go from being on TV to paying my rent in $1 bills, I didn't regret my decision.

Unfortunately, I quickly realized that the talent in Music City was far beyond any I'd come across in South Florida and surely, more than I was capable of as a self-professed Karaoke Queen and front woman of my Florida cover band!

From 2009-2012 I bounced between jobs in search of my purpose, a career that would allow me to utilize my talents, gifts and creativity and make a positive impact. My mother was a successful 'house-flipper' in our small town, Lanexa, Virginia. She was gracious enough to teach me her business, in loving support to help me keep my head above water! I flipped one or two houses a year but was never quite successful enough where I didn't need a day job. In 2010 I went against my mother's advice and purchased a loft in downtown Nashville, intending to flip it. 

In my 27 year old mind, sleeping on an air mattress in an empty loft, spending my free time listening to music in the bars just two blocks away was a pretty sweet gig. I was naive and ignorant to the fact that… it was 2010! Downtown properties were foreclosing faster than they were being purchased. My brilliant idea turned into my first failed flip. Between that and getting fired from a few jobs, my confidence was completely wrecked. 

My mom helped me furnish the loft, thinking staging the property would help it sell. Meanwhile, an acquaintance mentioned she'd listed her house on a web site and was renting it out nightly. As all of my personal belongings were packed up to move back home, tail between my legs and head low in utter defeat and self-loathing, my mom convinced me to use the last available funds on my credit card to list the loft online and, 'You never know. Maybe if you get a reservation you can get by for a little longer until you find your next job?'

In hindsight, I realize I actually failed my way forward. As I still kept finding jobs that would call me back to Nashville, but less optimistic that any of them would stick, I practically lived out of my car. When my loft was rented, I slept on friends' couches. If my loft was rented and I was again unemployed, I would travel to real estate seminars to make the most of my time. Eventually I realized that the career I had been searching for — an opportunity to build and grow a brand — was being met by my loft. 

I set to work finding a way to purchase more lofts in the building. I was passionate about creating the 'authentic Nashville experience' for my guests by providing a space that featured work from local artists and thereby, helping support my community. 
This passion has grown into something far beyond what I ever dreamed for myself or imagined possible. I never wanted to be a boss, I just wanted a job and one that I loved! I now have an entire team that not only loves Nashville, but deeply cares about helping our guests get the most from their visit. 

Our cleaning team is top-notch, as they understand all of the marketing we do on the front end means nothing if you walk in and aren't completely blown away! Our security team, Asset, are former military guys who not only provide comfort for our guests entering the building after a late night on the town but are extremely professional and courteous. We think it's awesome to have our guests looked after by 'Captain America!' 

On the reservations side, we have rockstars who truly care about your upcoming visit whether it be for a vacation, reunion, bachelorette party or conference. We not only want to give you an amazing space to call home and help you experience Nashville like a local, but we want to give you customized recommendations and resources so you fall in love with our city and want to come back again and again!

Suzanne is the head boss of guest experiences. She has been with the company since the beginning and you truly will not find someone more passionate about Nashville and its music scene. You're in the best hands! 

A little about how Suzanne and I came to work together, because I absolutely love telling this story — In 2012-2013 we were roommates. I was visiting with banks all day, trying to convince them that #TeamMCL was something to believe in (which at the time, had never before been seen at such scale in Nashville) and staying up all night answering e-mails and fulfilling reservations. Suzanne walked out of her home office (mine was the kitchen table) to tell me she was cut from her company in a corporate downsizing. Realizing I needed to not only get some sleep, but keep whatever little funds I had in-house so we could avoid eviction, I asked her if she wanted to work for #TeamMCL. Her classic response, which I will always remember, a very unenthusiastic, 'I guess I have to.' 
It's so comical to remember that day because while she begrudgingly agreed then, she is a total rockstar now!

Suzanne has grown to not only be an irreplaceable teammate, to whom I am forever grateful to helping me make this business possible not only in operations, but in the emotional support that I needed when times were really hard and no bank would give me the time of day, my mother's passing and my first business partner's ALS diagnosis (Former Tennessee Titan, Tim Shaw. Check out his book 'Blitz Your Life' because it's GREAT!), but she is a true champion of #TeamMCL and the authentic Nashville experience we are trying to provide for our guests. She maintains the properties to a high standard of expectations and she delights in hearing our guests' stories, connecting with them and giving them personalized recommendations of shows and events. A recommendation from her is like getting the 'inside scoop' on up-and-coming artists, so you can feel like one of the 'cool kids' when you come to town and get to experience Nashville like a true local!

My vision for #TeamMCL is this:
We aim to create a world-wide brand of privately owned vacation rentals, starting with the Music City, USA. The industry of private home rentals is extremely variable and uncertain. I have traveled and stayed in homes all over and have asked these very same questions. I have collected my own terrible experiences where the property wasn't as advertised, wasn't clean or I didn't feel safe. I have also stayed in places that didn't feel authentic, but were stale and run-of-the-mill, where I may have just as well stayed in a box-store hotel chain! Overall, the property you stay in can significantly impact the quality of your trip, your emotions, adventure, experience and ultimately, your memories! Knowing this and what I've learned through my own experiences and from our guests since renting out my first loft in 2011 before establishing #TeamMCL as a company, I have a dream to bring a standard of comfort, quality and consistency into the vacation rental world, all while creating spaces that are 'authentic' to that city by supporting local artists and reflecting that city's unique culture and vibe. 

More than being a successful company with a culture we can be proud of, we intend to be a force for good. We feel it's our mission to give back to our guests by delivering an exceptional experience where our guests feel genuinely cared for, but as a company we aim to do so much more to positively impact the world. We want our guests to know that while they are getting what they pay for and having an amazing experience worthy of a 5-Star review, a portion of their hard earned money is being paid forward toward a cause, whether it's ALS research, disadvantaged and orphaned children, or teen moms needing additional career education and encouragement.

Having faced personal struggle and the challenges of starting a company, coming through victoriously to other side, I truly believe that anything is possible!

Our core goals include:
* Setting the stage — Owning romantic real estate in romantic cities, all over the world
* WOWing our guests with cleanliness, quality and customer service — Creating a world-wide brand of vacation rentals that travelers can trust
* WOWing our guests by delighting five of their senses (Sight, Smell, Touch, Taste and Sound) through our properties and personalized recommendations of authentic, unique and local experiences
* Be WOW Memory Makers — WOW our guests so they can experience joy, delight and adventure, through our properties and recommendations so they can create memories they will cherish for a lifetime when they Stay {Somewhere} Awesome!
* Positively impact our Team, our guests and our community through passion, growth/learning and contribution

Thank you, in advance, for giving us the opportunity to meet our goals as a team. We are looking forward to serving you and earning your 5-Star Review. We live and die by them. If there's anything you need from us during your stay, please contact us so we have the opportunity to deliver! Also, word-of-mouth is essential for us to grow and thrive so if you loved staying at a #TeamMCL loft, please tell your friends! 

With Sincerity and Deep Appreciation,
Dani Dubetz

host_about:

Prior to moving to Nashville, I played volleyball for Florida International University and later worked as a news reporter for WPTV in West Palm Beach. I learned telling a sad story every day wasn't really 'my thing.' 

I moved to Nashville, like many, in pursuit of a music career, working as a beverage cart girl at a golf club, waitressing and coaching volleyball. As humbling as it was to go from being on TV to paying my rent in $1 bills, I didn't regret my decision.

Unfortunately, I quickly realized that the talent in Music City was far beyond any I'd come across in South Florida and surely, more than I was capable of as a self-professed Karaoke Queen and front woman of my Florida cover band!

From 2009-2012 I bounced between jobs in search of my purpose, a career that would allow me to utilize my talents, gifts and creativity and make a positive impact. My mother was a successful 'house-flipper' in our small town, Lanexa, Virginia. She was gracious enough to teach me her business, in loving support to help me keep my head above water! I flipped one or two houses a year but was never quite successful enough where I didn't need a day job. In 2010 I went against my mother's advice and purchased a loft in downtown Nashville, intending to flip it. 

In my 27 year old mind, sleeping on an air mattress in an empty loft, spending my free time listening to music in the bars just two blocks away was a pretty sweet gig. I was naive and ignorant to the fact that… it was 2010! Downtown properties were foreclosing faster than they were being purchased. My brilliant idea turned into my first failed flip. Between that and getting fired from a few jobs, my confidence was completely wrecked. 

My mom helped me furnish the loft, thinking staging the property would help it sell. Meanwhile, an acquaintance mentioned she'd listed her house on a web site and was renting it out nightly. As all of my personal belongings were packed up to move back home, tail between my legs and head low in utter defeat and self-loathing, my mom convinced me to use the last available funds on my credit card to list the loft online and, 'You never know. Maybe if you get a reservation you can get by for a little longer until you find your next job?'

In hindsight, I realize I actually failed my way forward. As I still kept finding jobs that would call me back to Nashville, but less optimistic that any of them would stick, I practically lived out of my car. When my loft was rented, I slept on friends' couches. If my loft was rented and I was again unemployed, I would travel to real estate seminars to make the most of my time. Eventually I realized that the career I had been searching for — an opportunity to build and grow a brand — was being met by my loft. 

I set to work finding a way to purchase more lofts in the building. I was passionate about creating the 'authentic Nashville experience' for my guests by providing a space that featured work from local artists and thereby, helping support my community. 
This passion has grown into something far beyond what I ever dreamed for myself or imagined possible. I never wanted to be a boss, I just wanted a job and one that I loved! I now have an entire team that not only loves Nashville, but deeply cares about helping our guests get the most from their visit. 

Our cleaning team is top-notch, as they understand all of the marketing we do on the front end means nothing if you walk in and aren't completely blown away! Our security team, Asset, are former military guys who not only provide comfort for our guests entering the building after a late night on the town but are extremely professional and courteous. We think it's awesome to have our guests looked after by 'Captain America!' 

On the reservations side, we have rockstars who truly care about your upcoming visit whether it be for a vacation, reunion, bachelorette party or conference. We not only want to give you an amazing space to call home and help you experience Nashville like a local, but we want to give you customized recommendations and resources so you fall in love with our city and want to come back again and again!

Suzanne is the head boss of guest experiences. She has been with the company since the beginning and you truly will not find someone more passionate about Nashville and its music scene. You're in the best hands! 

A little about how Suzanne and I came to work together, because I absolutely love telling this story — In 2012-2013 we were roommates. I was visiting with banks all day, trying to convince them that #TeamMCL was something to believe in (which at the time, had never before been seen at such scale in Nashville) and staying up all night answering e-mails and fulfilling reservations. Suzanne walked out of her home office (mine was the kitchen table) to tell me she was cut from her company in a corporate downsizing. Realizing I needed to not only get some sleep, but keep whatever little funds I had in-house so we could avoid eviction, I asked her if she wanted to work for #TeamMCL. Her classic response, which I will always remember, a very unenthusiastic, 'I guess I have to.' 
It's so comical to remember that day because while she begrudgingly agreed then, she is a total rockstar now!

Suzanne has grown to not only be an irreplaceable teammate, to whom I am forever grateful to helping me make this business possible not only in operations, but in the emotional support that I needed when times were really hard and no bank would give me the time of day, my mother's passing and my first business partner's ALS diagnosis (Former Tennessee Titan, Tim Shaw. Check out his book 'Blitz Your Life' because it's GREAT!), but she is a true champion of #TeamMCL and the authentic Nashville experience we are trying to provide for our guests. She maintains the properties to a high standard of expectations and she delights in hearing our guests' stories, connecting with them and giving them personalized recommendations of shows and events. A recommendation from her is like getting the 'inside scoop' on up-and-coming artists, so you can feel like one of the 'cool kids' when you come to town and get to experience Nashville like a true local!

My vision for #TeamMCL is this:
We aim to create a world-wide brand of privately owned vacation rentals, starting with the Music City, USA. The industry of private home rentals is extremely variable and uncertain. I have traveled and stayed in homes all over and have asked these very same questions. I have collected my own terrible experiences where the property wasn't as advertised, wasn't clean or I didn't feel safe. I have also stayed in places that didn't feel authentic, but were stale and run-of-the-mill, where I may have just as well stayed in a box-store hotel chain! Overall, the property you stay in can significantly impact the quality of your trip, your emotions, adventure, experience and ultimately, your memories! Knowing this and what I've learned through my own experiences and from our guests since renting out my first loft in 2011 before establishing #TeamMCL as a company, I have a dream to bring a standard of comfort, quality and consistency into the vacation rental world, all while creating spaces that are 'authentic' to that city by supporting local artists and reflecting that city's unique culture and vibe. 

More than being a successful company with a culture we can be proud of, we intend to be a force for good. We feel it's our mission to give back to our guests by delivering an exceptional experience where our guests feel genuinely cared for, but as a company we aim to do so much more to positively impact the world. We want our guests to know that while they are getting what they pay for and having an amazing experience worthy of a 5-Star review, a portion of their hard earned money is being paid forward toward a cause, whether it's ALS research, disadvantaged and orphaned children, or teen moms needing additional career education and encouragement.

host_about:

Prior to moving to Nashville, I played volleyball for Florida International University and later worked as a news reporter for WPTV in West Palm Beach. I learned telling a sad story every day wasn't really 'my thing.' 

I moved to Nashville, like many, in pursuit of a music career, working as a beverage cart girl at a golf club, waitressing and coaching volleyball. As humbling as it was to go from being on TV to paying my rent in $1 bills, I didn't regret my decision.

Unfortunately, I quickly realized that the talent in Music City was far beyond any I'd come across in South Florida and surely, more than I was capable of as a self-professed Karaoke Queen and front woman of my Florida cover band!

From 2009-2012 I bounced between jobs in search of my purpose, a career that would allow me to utilize my talents, gifts and creativity and make a positive impact. My mother was a successful 'house-flipper' in our small town, Lanexa, Virginia. She was gracious enough to teach me her business, in loving support to help me keep my head above water! I flipped one or two houses a year but was never quite successful enough where I didn't need a day job. In 2010 I went against my mother's advice and purchased a loft in downtown Nashville, intending to flip it. 

In my 27 year old mind, sleeping on an air mattress in an empty loft, spending my free time listening to music in the bars just two blocks away was a pretty sweet gig. I was naive and ignorant to the fact that… it was 2010! Downtown properties were foreclosing faster than they were being purchased. My brilliant idea turned into my first failed flip. Between that and getting fired from a few jobs, my confidence was completely wrecked. 

My mom helped me furnish the loft, thinking staging the property would help it sell. Meanwhile, an acquaintance mentioned she'd listed her house on a web site and was renting it out nightly. As all of my personal belongings were packed up to move back home, tail between my legs and head low in utter defeat and self-loathing, my mom convinced me to use the last available funds on my credit card to list the loft online and, 'You never know. Maybe if you get a reservation you can get by for a little longer until you find your next job?'

In hindsight, I realize I actually failed my way forward. Kate

host_about:
Hey y'all! My name is Dani Dubetz and I created my short-term rental business in 2012. 

Prior to moving to Nashville, I played volleyball for Florida International University and later worked as a news reporter for WPTV in West Palm Beach. I learned telling a sad story every day wasn't really 'my thing.' 

I moved to Nashville, like many, in pursuit of a music career, working as a beverage cart girl at a golf club, waitressing and coaching volleyball. As humbling as it was to go from being on TV to paying my rent in $1 bills, I didn't regret my decision.

Unfortunately, I quickly realized that the talent in Music City was far beyond any I'd come across in South Florida and surely, more than I was capable of as a self-professed Karaoke Queen and front woman of my Florida cover band!

From 2009-2012 I bounced between jobs in search of my purpose, a career that would allow me to utilize my talents, gifts and creativity and make a positive impact. My mother was a successful 'house-flipper' in our small town, Lanexa, Virginia. She was gracious enough to teach me her business, in loving support to help me keep my head above water! I flipped one or two houses a year but was never quite successful enough where I didn't need a day job. In 2010 I went against my mother's advice and purchased a loft in downtown Nashville, intending to flip it. 

In my 27 year old mind, sleeping on an air mattress in an empty loft, spending my free time listening to music in the bars just two blocks away was a pretty sweet gig. I was naive and ignorant to the fact that… it was 2010! Downtown properties were foreclosing faster than they were being purchased. My brilliant idea turned into my first failed flip. Between that and getting fired from a few jobs, my confidence was completely wrecked. 

My mom helped me furnish the loft, thinking staging the property would help it sell. Meanwhile, an acquaintance mentioned she'd listed her house on a web site and was renting it out nightly. As all of my personal belongings were packed up to move back home, tail between my legs and head low in utter defeat and self-loathing, my mom convinced me to use the last available funds on my credit card to list the loft online and, 'You never know. Maybe if you get a reservation you can get by for a little longer until you find your next job?'

In hindsight, I realize I actually failed my way forward. As I still kept finding jobs that would call me back to Nashville, but less optimistic that any of them would stick, I practically lived out of my car. When my loft was rented, I slept on friends' couches. If my loft was rented and I was again unemployed, I would travel to real estate seminars to make the most of my time. Eventually I realized that the career I had been searching for — an opportunity to build and grow a brand — was being met by my loft. 

I set to work finding a way to purchase more lofts in the building. I was passionate about creating the 'authentic Nashville experience' for my guests by providing a space that featured work from local artists and thereby, helping support my community. 
This passion has grown into something far beyond what I ever dreamed for myself or imagined possible. I never wanted to be a boss, I just wanted a job and one that I loved! I now have an entire team that not only loves Nashville, but deeply cares about helping our guests get the most from their visit. 

Our cleaning team is top-notch, as they understand all of the marketing we do on the front end means nothing if you walk in and aren't completely blown away! Our security team, Asset, are former military guys who not only provide comfort for our guests entering the building after a late night on the town but are extremely professional and courteous. We think it's awesome to have our guests looked after by 'Captain America!' 

On the reservations side, we have rockstars who truly care about your upcoming visit whether it be for a vacation, reunion, bachelorette party or conference. We not only want to give you an amazing space to call home and help you experience Nashville like a local, but we want to give you customized recommendations and resources so you fall in love with our city and want to come back again and again!

Suzanne is the head boss of guest experiences. She has been with the company since the beginning and you truly will not find someone more passionate about Nashville and its music scene. You're in the best hands! 

A little about how Suzanne and I came to work together, because I absolutely love telling this story — In 2012-2013 we were roommates. I was visiting with banks all day, trying to convince them that #TeamMCL was something to believe in (which at the time, had never before been seen at such scale in Nashville) and staying up all night answering e-mails and fulfilling reservations. Suzanne walked out of her home office (mine was the kitchen table) to tell me she was cut from her company in a corporate downsizing. Realizing I needed to not only get some sleep, but keep whatever little funds I had in-house so we could avoid eviction, I asked her if she wanted to work for #TeamMCL. Her classic response, which I will always remember, a very unenthusiastic, 'I guess I have to.' 
It's so comical to remember that day because while she begrudgingly agreed then, she is a total rockstar now!

Suzanne has grown to not only be an irreplaceable teammate, to whom I am forever grateful to helping me make this business possible not only in operations, but in the emotional support that I needed when times were really hard and no bank would give me the time of day, my mother's passing and my first business partner's ALS diagnosis (Former Tennessee Titan, Tim Shaw. Check out his book 'Blitz Your Life' because it's GREAT!), but she is a true champion of #TeamMCL and the authentic Nashville experience we are trying to provide for our guests. She maintains the properties to a high standard of expectations and she delights in hearing our guests' stories, connecting with them and giving them personalized recommendations of shows and events. A recommendation from her is like getting the 'inside scoop' on up-and-coming artists, so you can feel like one of the 'cool kids' when you come to town and get to experience Nashville like a true local!

My vision for #TeamMCL is this:
We aim to create a world-wide brand of privately owned vacation rentals, starting with the Music City, USA. The industry of private home rentals is extremely variable and uncertain. I have traveled and stayed in homes all over and have asked these very same questions. I have collected my own terrible experiences where the property wasn't as advertised, wasn't clean or I didn't feel safe. I have also stayed in places that didn't feel authentic, but were stale and run-of-the-mill, where I may have just as well stayed in a box-store hotel chain! Overall, the property you stay in can significantly impact the quality of your trip, your emotions, adventure, experience and ultimately, your memories! Knowing this and what I've learned through my own experiences and from our guests since renting out my first loft in 2011 before establishing #TeamMCL as a company, I have a dream to bring a standard of comfort, quality and consistency into the vacation rental world, all while creating spaces that are 'authentic' to that city by supporting local artists and reflecting that city's unique culture and vibe. 

More than being a successful company with a culture we can be proud of, we intend to be a force for good. We feel it's our mission to give back to our guests by delivering an exceptional experience where our guests feel genuinely cared for, but as a company we aim to do so much more to positively impact the world. We want our guests to know that while they are getting what they pay for and having an amazing experience worthy of a 5-Star review, a portion of their hard earned money is being paid forward toward a cause, whether it's ALS research, disadvantaged and orphaned children, or teen moms needing additional career education and encouragement.

Having faced personal struggle and the challenges of starting a company, coming through victoriously to other side, I truly believe that anything is possible!

Our core goals include:
* Setting the stage — Owning romantic real estate in romantic cities, all over the world
* WOWing our guests with cleanliness, quality and customer service — Creating a world-wide brand of vacation rentals that travelers can trust
* WOWing our guests by delighting five of their senses (Sight, Smell, Touch, Taste and Sound) through our properties and personalized recommendations of authentic, unique and local experiences
* Be WOW Memory Makers — WOW our guests so they can experience joy, delight and adventure, through our properties and recommendations so they can create memories they will cherish for a lifetime when they Stay {Somewhere} Awesome!
* Positively impact our Team, our guests and our community through passion, growth/learning and contribution

Thank you, in advance, for giving us the opportunity to meet our goals as a team. We are looking forward to serving you and earning your 5-Star Review. We live and die by them. If there's anything you need from us during your stay, please contact us so we have the opportunity to deliver! Also, word-of-mouth is essential for us to grow and thrive so if you loved staying at a #TeamMCL loft, please tell your friends! 

With Sincerity and Deep Appreciation,
Dani Dubetz

host_about:
For 35 years I was serving the world as a community organizer, artist, expressive arts facilitator, and traveler and then in for 20 years lived in a very large, beautiful home near Nashville with plenty of space for welcoming the world at the Morningstar House, before moving back to my hometown in southern Tennessee.  I have a passion for community building across lines of race, class, and culture and have found work on the boards and staff of many church and community non-profit organizations, locally, regionally and internationally.

I am the oldest grandchild in a large farm family in Southern Tennessee and learned the fine art of hospitality from my ancestors, especially warm-hearted grandmothers and great-grandmothers.  There was a great synergy and sustainability in the collective, cooperative work of my large family, and in the 15 years I lived in the "city" I brought this ethic and value to my life in community there.  

After 10 years of leadership in the forms of InterPlay, we formed and were practicing with MorningStar Community Arts, linking arts and social transformation, writing, and performing. I've written poetry all along the journey and am currently publishing an extensive audio collection with a title something like:  Radical Hospitality: Grief, Grace and Grits. 

I love to travel and have been to Morocco several times to stay with extended family there. Hawaii and Australia are favorites, too. I have 3 teenage grandchildren who grew up in the “red house” next to my “blue house” and now both houses are fully open for sharing extended stays with long term residents.  The houses are equipped for children of every age with art supplies, books, music, games, movies, etc.   

I always loved hosting house concerts, circle gatherings, and potlucks in my home and am enjoying taking this longtime  practice of hosting friends and family in my home to a new level with airbnb and other networks by hosting strangers that very often become friends. Since mid 2015, we made the shift at the Morningstar House to host guests for a 30 day minimum stay, so there's more continuity and just 3-4 guests sharing this huge home at any time. 
I spent 20 years traveling the world with my cultural work and my favorite way to visit any city is by doing a creative homestay with hosts that were sometimes friends, and sometimes friends of friends.  It's such a sweet way to come to know a city by having a safe, friendly, homey landing place. So that's what I want to offer now.  The spirit of hospitality comes naturally and easy to me.  My family used to say "I never met a stranger"  I really enjoy people in all their variety and would be happy to provide you a good balance of quiet and private time, and also friendly, helpful support as you encounter Nashville.

The new owner of my daughters “red house” Marquetta Dupree will be starting to offer expressive arts facilitation and support to guests interested in that, and possibly even collaborate with guests to create concerts, workshops and other events in the PlayRoom which holds about 55 people for a concert, and 30 for workshops.  For an affordable and hospitable way to live for your time in Nashville come and be a part of this community.

life motto:  "Sometimes you just have to take a leap and build your wings on the way down"..

See website at Morningstar Arts dot net.

John & Elisabeth

host_about:
Hi, my name is Mary Garrison. My husband Willie and I raised our children in east TN. We have lived on the west coast and the gulf coast. I have traveled on 3 continents. I have been traveling for work since 2001 and I am rarely in one place for long! We are dedicated and committed Tennesseans and always come home!  My favorite thing about traveling to other countries is to become immersed in local culture. That is why I love airbnb so much! I get to live in local homes for a short time. The most unusual places I have ever stayed are a castle in Scotland, a thatched roof, fisherman's cottage from the 1700s in Ireland, and an 400 square foot efficiency in Seoul, Korea.

My daughter and son-in-law have settled in Nashville and as a result, we have set up a household here to be close to them.  We hope you enjoy Nashville as much as we do! Check out the great brunch places close by! I go to a different place everyday: Dose, Nashville Biscuit House, Marche', Noshville. Whenever I am in town, I try to get in a walk through Shelby Park too just to walk off the biscuits! I try to catch live music whenever possible because there is always someone great to hear in Nashville. I highly recommend  catching any show at the Ryman where the acoustics are out of this world!

Finally, our neighbors are great. They are looking out for you and for us. If you see them, give a friendly wave and say hello. They have lived there for many years, and they have 4 generations stopping by to see them and check on them. They are the anchors of the neighborhood!

host_about:
Hello Fellow AirBnB Hosts and Travellers,

My husband Jonathan and I are delighted to have the opportunity to host honoured guests in our home.  I have always love being a hostess and this will enable me to enjoy this and meet some amazing new people along the way.  I hope our home brings you as much joy as it does for us.

A little background on our family.  Jonathan and I were married in May 2014 and we do not have any children.  Jonathan is from the Midlands of the UK and I grew up in French Canada (and therefore I speak fluent French) and lived in Minnesota as well.  We lived in South Carolina for several years and had the opportunity to host there, and hope to have the same wonderful experience here in Music City. Jonathan is only a recent transplant to the USA and can still be heard speaking with a lovely British accent.  Jon gets a kick out of how much us Americans fawn over his accent!  If you have no idea what he said...then he probably used a fancy English word that we don't use here, I am constantly discovering new words.

We both enjoy watching movies and use Netflix quite a bit!  Some of our most recent views include, Aquaman, and Watership Down.

 Jonathan is a professional musician and plays the bass trombone as his main instrument.  If you have ever wanted to see an enormous music library this is the place for you.  He has a small music studio lined with shelving covered with sheet music and over 900 CD's.  He is especially a Jazz lover, but has an incredible array of music available.  

I enjoy art of all types though I have not been able to invest as much in it as I like.  I also really enjoy Swing Dance and Lindy Hop.  Though I do not get to go very often, I can direct you to our local community should you wish to dance on Friday nights!Horses are another great love of mine, if I had the money and the space, I would have one of my own.

Before I forget, we don't have any children but we do have another very important member to our household: our cat Grace.  Grace is a beautiful calico that has never hurt a fly, she will be forever in your debt for a little bit of scratching and tends to be pretty quiet most of the time.  If you have cat allergies this is not the best place for you. Our guest room does have a closed door however.

In our home we hope to make your stay as comfy as your home, while offering as many hotel amenities as possible.   For the caffeine lovers of the world, a coffee pot will be available whenever you need it.  For those that are more of a tea persuasion, Jonathan can show you how to make a true British pot of tea.

Hope to have the pleasure of hosting you soon.

Sarah and Jonathan

host_about:
Jim and I are retirement age, have lived on this little cul de sac next door to the AirBnB property for over 20 years. I continue working with a small private practice as a psychiatric nurse practitioner. We live quietly, enjoying our three dogs and friends.  Jim is the extrovert, enjoys socializing and playing golf.  I'm the introvert preferring my books, dogs, and alone time. 
We hope to offer people who enjoy our property a beautiful, peaceful home with our support to make your visit a memorable experience. We will never be intrusive but we are nearby to answer any questions and any support to make your vacation so amazing you will want to return again and again. 
Nashville needs no introduction. Jim is a native of Nashville and I have lived here thirty years. It's just a fascinating place with endless things to do. It's not uncommon to run into a country music star while you are out and about. Please allow them their privacy unless they are in a venue that invites interaction. 
Nashville is so much more than country music though. There are probably more colleges and universities here than any other town this size. I think this reflects itself in the high quality people you find next door, down the street, or at the check-out line in the grocery. 
Then there's the world-class medical facilities. People come from all over for treatment plus a lot of research is is done here. Sarah Cannon (Minnie Peal) for cancer and Vanderbilt University Medical Center multiple disorders.
Don't forget, we are serous animal lovers.

name: Daybed in Playroom-open NOW-semi-private
description: NOW OPEN— price reduced.. $800 pr month…This listing is for a daybed in an open, semi-private playroom on the back of the Morningstar House.  It’s a comfortable transition space where you could stay while waiting for a room to open in either this house or our friends house next door.. there’s very little traffic through the room, and it’s a huge house so it’s easy to share with other monthly guests..
host_about:
For 35 years I was serving the world as a community organizer, artist, expressive arts facilitator, and traveler and then in for 20 years lived in a very large, beautiful home near Nashville with plenty of space for welcoming the world at the Morningstar House, before moving back to my hometown in southern Tennessee.  I have a passion for community building across lines of race, class, and culture and have found work on the boards and staff of many church and community non-profit organizations, locally, regionally and internationally.

I am the oldest grandchild in a large farm family in Southern Tennessee and learned the fine art of hospitality from my ancestors, especially warm-hearted grandmothers and great-grandmothers.  There was a great synergy and sustainability in the collective, cooperative work of my large family, and in the 15 years I lived in the "city" I brought this ethic and value to my life in community there.  

After 10 years of leadership in the forms of InterPlay, we formed and were practicing with MorningStar Community Arts, linking arts and social transformation, writing, and performing. I've written poetry all along the journey and am currently publishing an extensive audio collection with a title something like:  Radical Hospitality: Grief, Grace and Grits. 

I love to travel and have been to Morocco several times to stay with extended family there. Hawaii and Australia are favorites, too. I have 3 teenage grandchildren who grew up in the “red house” next to my “blue house” and now both houses are fully open for sharing extended stays with long term residents.  The houses are equipped for children of every age with art supplies, books, music, games, movies, etc.   

I always loved hosting house concerts, circle gatherings, and potlucks in my home and am enjoying taking this longtime  practice of hosting friends and family in my home to a new level with airbnb and other networks by hosting strangers that very often become friends. Since mid 2015, we made the shift at the Morningstar House to host guests for a 30 day minimum stay, so there's more continuity and just 3-4 guests sharing this huge home at any time. 
I spent 20 years traveling the world with my cultural work and my favorite way to visit any city is by doing a creative homestay with hosts that were sometimes friends, and sometimes friends of friends.  It's such a sweet way to come to know a city by having a safe, friendly, homey landing place. So that's what I want to offer now.  The spirit of hospitality comes naturally and easy to me.  My family used to say "I never met a stranger"  I really enjoy people in all their variety and would be happy to provide you a good balance of quiet and private time, and also friendly, helpful support as you encounter Nashville.

The new owner of my daughters “red house” Marquetta Dupree will be starting to offer expressive arts facilitation and support to guests interested in that, and possibly even collaborate with guests to create concerts, workshops and other events in the PlayRoom which holds about 55 people for a concert, and 30 for workshops.  For an affordable and hospitable way to live for your time in Nashville come and be a part of this community.

life motto:  "Sometimes you just have to take a leap and build your wings on the way down"..

See website at Morningstar Arts dot net.

description:

Permit# 2083509
host_about:
Hello Air BnB family!

My name is Mike (aka SavasONtheGo) and one of my passions in life is creating themed Air BnBs around the world. 

Currently, I have 3 properties(but I am on a mission to own more). Each one of them has its own flare and custom identity which takes into account the local culture and ethos of the area.  
Here's a summary:
1. Nashville, TN - Big Blue; A large home designed especially for groups and themed as a homage to Country Music and Rock N' Roll!
2. Missoula, MT - The Wooly Bungalow; a super comfy 3 bedroom home that incorporates American Native themes with modern-day design.
3. Porto, Portugal - The Port'hole Penthouse; a fully custom penthouse apartment overlooking the historic center's main square designed like an 18th century Captain's ship!

Normally, I am working in the music industry helping artists create and manage their touring VIP & Hospitality programs. Some of the acts I have worked with are The Rolling Stones, Bon Jovi, Metallica, Guns N' Roses, Cat Stevens, Phil Collins, Prince, Katy Perry, Eminem, Oprah, and Hugh Jackman.  When I am not on tour or producing high-end events, I am generally traveling the world on an epic adventure, competing in Marathons and Triathlons, or bouncing between my family members who miss me:) 

Needless to say, I OBSESS about the customer experience and get incredibly excited about creating environments that others connect with and which uplifts them.  My only hope is that when staying in one of my homes, you feel like you are in a special space created with the local culture and history in mind, combined with a delicate eye towards design and functionality.

Now, here's a bit more background on each of the properties (if you care):

Big Blue (Nashville):

We are two friends who met in 2008 while on tour with Bon Jovi (and lived on the same tour bus). Originally from New Jersey and Vermont, we now call Nashville home and decided to purchase this dream property in 2015 with one goal in mind; to create the most epic, eclectic, and badass Rock N roll home Nashville has ever seen! We both tour professionally and are constantly on tour with different artists - from The Zac Brown Band to Kid Rock to Oprah. description:
Studio apartment in Donelson in a well established neighborhood and is a perfect 30 day rental.

host_about:
I have been in my home for nearly 30 years and love my neighborhood and yard.  It was a wonderful place for my sons to grow up, now I would like to share it.  The flat was first a ‘rec-room’, then a bedroom for my oldest, followed by youngest. They have both since grown and started lives of their own.  In April ’15 I decided to transform the space into a sweet little apartment for an Airbnb. I remodeled and installed a new stainless steel stove, dishwasher and refrigerator.  French doors open up to a private and quiet yard that I am sure you will find very peaceful and only 15 minutes from all the action downtown!
I love meeting people, traveling and spending time with family.  In addition, I enjoy designing and decorating cakes as a hobby…it is my creative outlet.  
I also love animals and have two cats, Sterling and LeeLoo.  You will more than likely see Sterling casually strolling around his domain.  Little LeeLoo, however is very shy and hides inside most of the time.  You may see, as you drink your morning coffee, our resident ground hog, Miss Gwendalyn and deer that come to visit. 
Come stay in my Tranquil Flat, close to all the action Nashville has to offer as well as the peace that comes with secluded garden.

host_about:
My husband and I moved to East Nashville in 2017 after completing a work assignment in London and graduate school in Paris. We've been lucky to travel the world and have a global network of friends, which come together to make up our melange of style, food preferences, and personalities.

We're self-proclaimed nerds and runners (I'm not sure if those two things are related, but we have that in common!). I personally am always toting around a book, dog-eared and annotated to pieces. We met many years ago in a Boston running club so have always loved experiencing new geographies and bonding with new friends by foot. 

Like I said, we're lucky to be experienced travelers, so I have my perfect day of exploring down to a science. I wake up before anyone else and sneak out to a coffee shop for some precious alone time and journaling. After breakfast and a run or yoga, I'll politely require :) that my husband joins me for hours of boutique-browsing to take in that city's design style, and I find one special momento to add to my global wardrobe. Then, we wrap up the day with a great meal (the only planning I will have done for the trip), a couple glasses of wine, and an early bedtime.
